match.reason: None of the bank points covers the internal structure of a gene (promoter, exons, introns and the triplet code); the closest, Genomes, genes and alleles, only defines a gene as a section of DNA that codes for a product.

draft.title: Gene structure
card: A gene is a section of DNA that carries the instructions for making a polypeptide or a functional RNA. It has a start region and a body made of different parts.
a DNA sequence at the start of a gene. RNA polymerase binds here to begin copying the gene. The promoter is not part of the coding body.
a part of the gene that codes for the polypeptide. Exons stay in the final mRNA and are read in triplets.
a part of the gene that does not code for the polypeptide. Introns are copied at first, then removed from the RNA before it is read.
draft.remember: Promoter: where copying starts. Exons code and stay. Introns are removed.

a.q: Which part of a gene is the site where RNA polymerase binds to begin copying?
a.why: RNA polymerase binds to the promoter, which sits at the start of the gene. Exons are the coding parts that stay in the final mRNA, so they are not the binding site.
a.clue: Think of the region at the start that is not part of the coding body.

b.q: A gene in a human cell has three exons and two introns. Which statement about the finished RNA that is read to make the polypeptide is correct?
opts: It contains the three exons but not the two introns
It contains the two introns but not the three exons
It contains all five sections of the gene
It contains the promoter and the three exons
b.why: Exons code for the polypeptide and stay in the final RNA. Introns are removed before the RNA is read. The promoter only helps start copying and is not part of the coding body.
b.clue: Which sections code, and which are removed?

b.best: It contains the three exons but not the two introns
